title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is building the moduli of elliptic curves over S_0 = Spec Z[1/2] using Legendre-Jacobi 'épinglages' (pinnings). A pinning puts the curve in Legendre form y^2 = x(x-1)(x-λ) with λ in U_{0,3} = P^1 \ {0,1,∞}, together with an auxiliary primitive 4th root of unity. The corresponding moduli scheme is U_{0,3} ×_{S_0} μ_4^*, where μ_4^* is the scheme of primitive 4th roots of unity, Spec Z[1/2][i].

The group S_3 × μ_4 changes the pinning, and so acts on this scheme as follows (end of p.88 and start of this page).
- S_3 acts tautologically on U_{0,3} = P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, by permuting the three points, i.e. through λ ↦ 1-λ, 1/λ, and so on.
- On μ_4^* = {i, -i}, the element (g, ζ) acts by multiplication by the mixed character sg(g)·ζ^2 ∈ {±1}.
- Geometric reason for the sign twist: an odd permutation such as x ↦ 1-x changes the sign of the cubic. It must then be compensated by y ↦ ±iy, which flips the chosen i.

The subgroup acting trivially on μ_4^* is the kernel of (g, ζ) ↦ sg(g)ζ^2. This is the fibre product (48): D'_{3,S_0} = S_3 ×_{μ_2} μ_4, taken over the maps sgn : S_3 → μ_2 and squaring : μ_4 → μ_2.

Grothendieck then changes base to S̃_0 = μ_4^* (i.e. Z[1/2, i]). There μ_4^* acquires a canonical section i, and μ_4 ≅ Z/4. So D'_3 becomes the constant group (49): S_3 ×_{Z/2} Z/4, of order 12. It is a central extension (50): 1 → {±1} → D'_3 → D_3 ≅ S_3 → 1.

Over S̃_0, with i fixed, he begins to define 'direct' pinnings: those whose induced section of μ_4^* is exactly i. The next page states that direct pinnings are represented by U_{0,3, S̃_0}, with modular group D'_3 acting on them. The purpose is to make explicit the modular group action, including on the bundle O(1) (presumably weight-1 forms or the Hodge bundle) of the Legendre family. This is a careful scheme-theoretic version of the classical λ-function / S_3 ≅ SL_2(Z)/Γ(2) picture.
errors: Unremarked fact: the extension (50) is non-split. Every lift of a transposition is (τ, ±i), of order 4. So D'_3 is the dicyclic (binary dihedral) group Dic_3 ≅ Z/3 ⋊ Z/4 of order 12, consistent with the notation D'_3. Grothendieck does not name it or note the non-splitting on this page.

ideas.what: S_3 action on the Legendre λ-line, twisted on μ_4^* by the character sgn(g)·ζ^2 so as to act on Legendre pinnings including a choice of i
ideas.modern_name: anharmonic group action on the modular curve X(2) / Legendre family; descent from λ-line to j-line
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Legendre, Jacobi; λ-function theory); scheme-theoretic treatment e.g. Deligne-Rapoport, Katz-Mazur

ideas.what: Kernel subgroup S_3 ×_{μ_2} μ_4, which over Z[1/2,i] becomes the constant group S_3 ×_{Z/2} Z/4, a non-split central extension of S_3 by ±1
ideas.modern_name: binary dihedral / dicyclic group Dic_3 of order 12 as automorphism group of rigidified Legendre structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical group theory; its appearance with Legendre forms and level 2/4 structures is folklore

ideas.what: Base change to μ_4^* to 'rigidify' the sign ambiguity and define 'direct' pinnings representable by U_{0,3} over Z[1/2,i]
ideas.modern_name: rigidification / representability of moduli of elliptic curves with Legendre structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Igusa, Deligne-Rapoport, Katz-Mazur (moduli with level structure)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine working-out of the classical S_3 symmetry of the Legendre family over Z[1/2]. It identifies the order-12 dicyclic extension needed once a √-1 is involved. Nothing here appears beyond standard modular-curve folklore.
transcription_corrections: In the brace display, the first line reads 'μ_{4S}^* muni d'une section canonique i_S'. The '≃' after μ_{4S}^* is struck out in the manuscript.
(48) subscript: (S_3)_{S_0} ×_{μ_{2,S_0}} (μ_4)_{S_0}. This is the fibre product over μ_2, matching the image.
'sur ces schémas /S̃_0/ universels': the /S̃_0/ is an insertion above the line, probably meaning '(sur S̃_0) universels'.
Struck passage near the bottom: roughly 'Dans le sub[?] ... ie. un S_3 × μ_4'. It is crossed out and should be read as deleted.
